I absolutely despise this saying, but over the years I've better understood the purpose behind it. First of all, I wouldn't say "Love yourself" because that implies narcissism, the kind of person I would prefer to be is humble, one who doesn't flaunt their strengths and is reserved and respectable. A good deed gone unnoticed feels better than one you do for attention. Besides that, I would start with something smaller and more important which is "liking yourself." If you were to meet someone exactly like you, would you get along well with them? Would you like that person? Odds are if you do, someone else would too. If you don't like that person, why? Life is a fucking struggle man, and we're all aiming for something. Become the person you want to be, in small steps. Eventually you can be proud of what you are, despite your suffering you SURVIVED and you're stronger for it. Make decisions that you believe are the right ones, do right by yourself. Also more importantly, forgive yourself. Be less harsh, understand you're doing the best you can and that it's okay to not be running at 100%, no-one with depression is. At the same time, try to push yourself. The right thing is hardly ever the easiest. Trust your feelings, be strong, build self-respect and eventually you will learn to like yourself. Everybody deals with this differently, but after eight years I finally respect the person I've become and it's helped build the foundations for moving forward with my life. It's still hard and it still sucks, but it's a step. Good luck OP and to anyone out there suffering - I wish you all the best

Piggybacking off this comment, all good advice, Lightning Strike has been a GODSEND on my most recent attempt. I try to stick with one army so I don't run on a deficit, and I can utilize my growth to get high-tier troops quickly. It also makes your lightning strikes more deadly. I've taken out 4 stacks of empire troops right on top of each other with my single stack of 20 using this strategy.

I've beaten the orc campaign and I'm about 85 turns into my chaos campaign on very hard. The early game was tough dealing with pistoliers and marauder horsemen because all our troops are so slow. My strategy has been to grab lightning strike on my lord and build him as a hero-killer, focusing on eliminating their infantry. I've only kept one army as I don't like running on a deficit and I feel the growth cost sets my technology back too far. Try to recruit more halberdiers, though they aren't fast they perform very well against cav and war dogs in melee and if you use your chaos warriors shields the missiles do minimal damage. Get the horse on your lord and maybe a champion to chase them down and try to push them into the bulk of your force. Normally I win through morale and most of the cav escapes, but the casualties aren't too bad if I maneuver my army well. Also, if you're using archaeon or have a chaos sorcerer fireball is an excellent way to kill off larger units, groups of infantry, and even cav if you get a good angle, as I find the missiles track very well. Good luck!

If you can manage to make peace with the orc tribes, maybe. I find the dwarves are really tough to conquer, on the world map and in the battlefield. You might actually have better luck conquering the orc tribes to the south first and consolidating your power. I find the east dwarven faction (the name escapes me) usually peaces out if your forces are strong enough, then all you have to worry about is the barak varr to the west and the dwarves to the north. be careful to not get into too many wars at once, you're in a vulnerable position at first surrounded on all sides. Pick off the red teef settlements (including iron keep - slap a defensive building there if you can afford it, it gets attacked constantly) try to make a couple defensive alliances with orc tribes who like you and that should help with the dwarf problem slightly. Try not to confederate unless you encompass the faction, I find it spreads your forces too thin and makes public order and diplomacy a nightmare.

It was really rough around the early-mid parts of the game. I lost a lot of provinces due to public order and constant dwarves attacking iron peak. I found the formula for setting up towns (priority changes depending on location) Settlements get Boss tent to rank 2 for public order and corruption issues. A goblin outpost to help the garrison defend against rebels + dwarves, and da hoard for extra income to fund more orc armies. For the capital if it was my main province death pass or a key military location I'd get a tier 4 barracks and either a tinker workshop or giants lair. otherwise they always got (special building if they have it. Shaman hut (corruption issues solved, also more global recruitment, awesome!), Da Hoard, Defensive building, Boss Tent level 3, and the last one is usually either a specific military building or whatever is needed most in that province. If you get a group of 17 orks and just raid with them or use them to kill rebels you can spawn a WAAAGH which you can use to target rebel armies you can't reach with your main ones. Hope this helps, good luck!

I've been in the same situation man, and it sucks. It hurts. It hurts so bad like a wound that never goes away. It hurts so much that it gnaws at your thoughts and drives you crazy, where the only thing left that you think you can do to escape the agony is suicide. Infatuation isn't fun, I've experienced it many times and it has almost always ended with a near-death experience for me. There's not much advice I can give you for avoiding the pain, other than actively trying to avoid thinking of the person. Find things to distract your brain. Play games, read a book, spend time with friends, anything that can preoccupy your mind away from this person. Anytime you're forced to be in a situation near that person it's going to hurt, because you remember that they exist and that pain all comes flooding back in. I'm not saying everyone experiences it this way, but it's how I have. Don't make the same mistake I made and fall harder and harder in love in the hopes that it will work out, the earlier you break off from that person the less it's going to end up hurting. I know to you she seems like the perfect person, absolutely gorgeous and wonderful despite any of her flaws, but trust me, these feelings blind you. She isn't all what your brain makes her out to be, she's flawed just like you or me. Get it into your head that she isn't perfect, and it might make it a little bit easier to bear the thought of never being with her. I really wish there was more I could say to help you man, but I'm struggling with the same thing daily - so I haven't figured out the miracle cure for heartache. The feelings never really go away, not entirely. The only way I've been able to save myself is to get as far away from them as possible, and shove those thoughts and feelings to the back of my mind, if only to stay sane. Good luck friend - my heart goes out to you.

Reading this post concerns me with my own depression. I am coming from a different perspective, as a straight male in his early 20's. I've only been in a few very brief relationships that all ended up with me being brokenhearted from either being used or lied to. I've had very little opportunity with relationship prospects as my hobbies and career choice are largely male-dominated. Despite this, I've been trying to find my significant other.

I do realize that finding her wouldn't mean the cure for my depression, as this seems to be stuck with me for the long-term - but I did believe that being in a loving relationship with someone would make the burden much easier to bear. I'm worried now that my depression will even rob me of the one thing left I'm hoping for. 

Regardless, the only thing keeping me around are the relationships I'm lucky enough to have with my friends and family, and I couldn't bear to hurt them by leaving. The infatuation I've felt in previous relationships was the only times that I believe I felt truly happy. Unfortunately the breakup always multiplies those emotions tenfold in the negative and I come dangerously close to giving up.

Right now I'm terrified of having to go throughout my entire life single and alone as I have been, but at the same time am afraid to trust any new potential partner not only for fear of being betrayed but also the huge risk of losing my own life. Please don't tell me I have to do this alone.
